answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a bond each agent locks in a vault before it may attest. The stake is tied to one address, so a thousand fake agents need a thousand bonds; cost grows with every alias. Caught double-signing, the bond is slashed, so the attacker loses principal and reward. Because the vault reads a shared ledger, a fresh identity cannot reset the price. Even a well-behaved fake pays the opportunity cost of idle capital. The cedar stake and the timber behind it are a real expense: ten fake votes cost ten bonds, so Sybil stops paying.
